title: Last offices, laying out, and care after death as dignity work

source_packet.source_basis: Public-source practice-layer synthesis for schema testing; no private testimony, no contributor interview, no claim of corpus completeness.
limitations: Public sources describe recognized care patterns but do not supply firsthand room texture.
This record must not become procedure-level instruction for a particular death.
Treatment, legal, ritual, emergency, and equipment decisions remain local and must be handled by qualified teams or relevant authorities.

moment.plain_scene: After death, trained carers, family, or funeral workers may wash, position, cover, dress, or otherwise care for the body, while preserving wishes, ritual, modesty, and local policy.

content_layers.observation_text: Professional and public sources describe care after death as preserving dignity, following wishes and care plans, respecting cultural/religious needs, and involving appropriate trained staff or family as permitted.
content_layers.source_synthesis: Marie Curie’s professional care-after-death material gives this record a stronger practice footing, while public sources show the family-facing version of the same threshold.

interpretation.editor_interpretation: This record makes after-death body care part of the bedside corpus rather than an administrative afterthought. It holds the body as a person’s body, not a problem to remove.

what_this_is_not: not permission to perform restricted religious or cultural practices without authority
not a universal manual for washing, dressing, moving, or closing the mouth/eyes
not legal advice about keeping a body at home
not a substitute for infection-control, medical-device, or funeral guidance
uncertainties: Family participation, professional responsibility, infection-control rules, and rituals vary.
Some practices are tradition-governed and should remain off-record unless authorized.
Future records need funeral director, nurse, care-aide, and family testimony.
content_layers.lay_orientation: A lay surface should say that care after death exists, may include wishes and rituals, and should be guided by the care team, funeral staff, local law, and the family’s tradition.
content_layers.practitioner_notes: A practitioner surface should collect how to ask about wishes, how to protect modesty, how to invite or decline family participation, and when not to force mouth/eye closure.
language_notes: Define “last offices” without assuming all readers know it.
Respect “exists” versus “is yours to see” for rituals.

provenance.provenance_statement: Drafted from named public sources to test the practice layer. It should be reviewed before any public surface uses it.

safety.clinical_boundary: This record is observational/source-indexing only. It is not medical advice, not a prognosis, not a legal instruction, not a ritual authority, and not a substitute for a local hospice, clinician, emergency, legal, cultural, or care team.
safety.safety_notes: Before public use, route through clinical or domain review and ensure any lay surface directs urgent, worried, legal, medication, swallowing, equipment, or body-handling questions to qualified local support.
